extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, journalists, and media scholars interested in how press releases function as information subsidies
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist- and theory-based framework for evaluating how well a press release functions as an "information subsidy" that lowers journalists' costs and thus increases the likelihood of pickup. Focuses on concrete ways a release can reduce search, verification, production, cognitive, and editorial costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information subsidy (Gandy's definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An information subsidy is an effort by means of which information in a form suitable for processing by the mass media is provided to those media in a controlled manner at a subsidized cost."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational framing: a press release is evaluated by how well it supplies information in media-ready form and thereby lowers the marginal cost for journalists to produce a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the release in a form the newsroom can publish with minimal rewriting (inverted-pyramid lead, AP-style, clean quotes, embargoed for the relevant cycle)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific expectations: lead written in inverted-pyramid style, copy conforms to common newsroom/style conventions (e.g., AP), quotes are clear and attribution-ready, and embargo language (when used) matches the reporters' publishing cycle. Anti-patterns: verbose, non-newslead intros, or copy requiring substantial re-editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-cost reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release supply the underlying study/PDF/dataset so a reporter does not have to hunt for it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct links or attachments to source documents (studies, data, reports). The easier it is for a reporter to access primary materials, the lower their time expenditure and the higher pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification-cost reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Are named sources reachable, with phone/email and time-zone availability windows? Are statistics already attributed to citable sources?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact information for spokespeople/experts, clear availability windows, and precise attributions for facts and figures to enable quick fact-checking. Anti-patterns: vague source descriptions or unreachable spokespeople.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production-cost reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Are images, graphics, B-roll, broadcast-quality audio, and pull quotes pre-supplied with usage rights cleared?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality multimedia assets with explicit usage permissions/licenses and suggested cutlines or captions. This reduces newsroom production time and legal clearance burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive-cost reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the angle, the "so what," and the contextualization done — so the reporter doesn't have to invent a frame?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a clear news hook, suggested framings, and contextual background that situates the announcement within larger trends or controversies. Avoid leaving reporters to devise the basic narrative or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of editorial uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release flag what is new, what is unique, what makes the story defensible to an editor (e.g., peer-reviewed, embargoed, exclusive)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly call out novelty, exclusivity, peer review status, and other defensibility signals that help editors judge whether the story merits space. Use of embargoes or confirmed exclusives can reduce editorial risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the subsidy directed to the right journalist (beat match), at the right time (deadline-aligned)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute to reporters who cover the relevant beat and time the release to align with newsroom cycles/deadlines. Mass, untargeted blasts or poorly timed sends increase search and editorial costs and reduce pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource-asymmetry / fairness caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidy effectiveness is partly a function of the resources of the source — well-funded subsidizers (corporations, large universities, government) crowd out resource-poor sources (small NGOs, marginal communities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative warning: assess whether the release is merely aiding journalism or is skewing coverage through production-budget advantage. For evaluators, consider an additional fairness dimension: does the subsidy manipulate coverage by sheer resource advantage?

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness (operational implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A release that fully subsidizes the cost of a story — facts, quotes, images, embargoed exclusive, contactable expert — will be picked up at much higher rates than one that merely announces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational definition: pickup-worthiness is a function of how successfully the release lowers the marginal cost of running the story. Use the above checklist items as measurable levers for predicting or improving pickup rates.
